findings.title: canManage() grants manage on groups to admins holding only the view scope
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the caller only has the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type. `canManage()` backs `requireManage()` used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, so an admin granted only all-groups `view` can create top-level groups. The scope list should contain only `MANAGE` (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79, which correctly uses only `MANAGE`).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In V2, the authz resource created for a group is named with the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name), while `resource.getId()` is an unrelated resource UUID. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and that set is stored as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. With wrong ids, the store-level filtering/count matches no groups, so user counts are reported as 0 and group-scoped user queries return nothing. Use `groupResource.getName()`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes a resource id into hasPermission(groupId, ...)
findings.body: `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, but here it is called with `groupResource.getId()` (a resource UUID), not the resource name/group id. The lookup therefore always returns null and the code falls back to the `Groups` resource-type ("all groups") resource, so per-group view-members permissions are never detected and the method returns an empty or incorrect set. Pass `groupResource.getName()` (or refactor to evaluate the already-loaded resource).

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: If `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null (it returns null when the authorization schema is not supported for the resource server, or when the resource type resource is missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` is called with a null resource and `resource.getScopes()` is dereferenced at line 152, causing a NullPointerException instead of a clean deny. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. Group permissions store the group id as the resource name, so for `Groups` permissions this now falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is not set for these resources and will typically be null — the admin console will show no/blank resource name for group permissions. Add a `Groups` branch resolving the group path/name (and "All groups" for the type resource).

findings.title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers refers to the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Also `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while its return type is `Set<String>`.

findings.title: Removal of public ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes breaks extensions
findings.body: `searchGroupModelsByAttributes` was a public static method on `ModelToRepresentation` in server-spi-private; deleting it is a source/binary incompatible change for any provider or downstream code calling it. Consider deprecating and delegating instead of removing outright, or note the removal in upgrade docs.
